summary: Auguste Comte was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and at École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle served as Direttore at Aliah University (circa 1881–1899) and secretary at The Asiatic Society in 1891.

Awadh Kishore Narain worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS, later serving as professor at BHU and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Klein is a scholar of Japanology who studied at the University of Bonn. He worked at Bonn (1998–2007), the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and became a professor at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha, earned degrees at Hamburg and Kiel, and held professorships at the University of Bern (1992–1996) and Heidelberg University from 1996.
Ayako Nakamura works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

Ayu Khandro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. She studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa, and taught Namkhai Norbu and A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé.

Ayya Khema was active in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under teachers including Phra Khantipalo, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Matara Sri Ñāṇārāma, founded Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978, and taught at Buddha-Haus in 1989.
Azizah Nur is a doctoral student attested at the Australian National University in 2026, studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teachers and at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt, taught at Tibet Institute Rikon and UCSB, and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

B. B. Lal was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Allahabad and under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of IIAS (1976–1986).

B. N. K. Sharma worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha and at the University of Madras and Presidency College, later serving at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, and Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College (1953–1969).

B. R. Ambedkar worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia under Dewey, Seligman, Shotwell, and Robinson, and at LSE under Cannan and Mackinder, later holding posts at Sydenham College, Government Law College, and Ramjas College.

id: P:Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel
summary: Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Baatr U. Kitinov works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a PhD from Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology, studying at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966) and became a professor at Panjab University around 1965.

Bai Su worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Peking University under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and served as a professor at Peking University from 1948 to 2004.
Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (circa 1915–1918) and held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (circa 1946–1958), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (circa 1958–1978), and the Institute of Philosophy at CASS (circa 1978–2014).

Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow from circa 1956 to 1976.
